questions.q: What is said about the name Muhammad in the world today?
options: It is the most given name, and it is Nabi's haters who are cut off
questions.explain: The Prophet's name is not cut off.

questions.q: What four labels did Quraysh throw at the Prophet SAW?
questions.explain: They labelled him even though they knew he was honest.

questions.q: What did Al-Walid do although he admitted the Quran is not human speech?
options: Rejected it because of vested interests
questions.explain: Knowing the truth does not mean accepting it.

questions.q: Why did Umar become open to the Quran according to this lecture?
options: He heard the recitation directly himself
questions.explain: Most opponents never heard the real message.

questions.q: The Prophet's character was successfully destroyed by personal attacks.
questions.explain: False. No one who dealt with him found a flaw.

questions.q: A weak hadith is the same as a fabricated hadith.
questions.explain: False. A daif hadith has a weak chain but is not fabricated.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: The phase of physical torture begins
Abu Lahab celebrates the death of the Prophet's son
Al-Walid is persuaded to deny the Quran

questions.explain: Al-Kawthar came down, labels were thrown, followers were mocked, Al-Walid was persuaded, and physical torture began.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: Pulling someone's reputation down from public acceptance

questions.explain: Al-Kawthar is abundant goodness, abtar is cut off, cancel is toppling a reputation, and inferiority complex is a lasting sense of inferiority.

questions.q: The more labels are thrown, what happens to people?
options: They grow wary without hearing the real message
questions.explain: Beware of labels as a tactic.
